prompt: State two differences between dry solid kinetic friction and viscous drag in a fluid.

mark_scheme.criterion: Solid kinetic friction is approximately independent of speed, whereas viscous drag increases as speed increases.
Fluid drag is zero when stationary, whereas solid static friction can be non-zero (or drag depends strongly on frontal area and shape, whereas solid friction is largely independent of surface area).

hints: Consider how each force depends on speed.
Consider the value of each force when the object is stationary, or their dependence on area/shape.
solution: 1. Solid kinetic friction is approximately independent of speed, whereas fluid drag increases as speed increases. 2. Fluid drag is zero when stationary, whereas solid friction can exist at zero speed as static friction.
teacher_walkthrough: Award B1 for contrasting speed dependence.
Award B1 for contrasting zero-speed behavior (or cross-sectional area/streamlining dependence).
Each difference must be clearly paired between solids and fluids.
